messages:
elaine: Hey team — docs PR #482 is blocked. The config example shows `preferred_model: 'redwood-7b'` plus `fallback_models: ['redwood-2b-quant', 'gptx-lite']` but we didn't explain runtime routing priority across hosted / dedicated / private. Need runtime confirmation before we merge. Also the Python SDK streaming snippet might give a false impression about client cancel actually stopping work server-side. @samir @maria can you weigh in?
samir: Can you paste the exact snippet you used in the PR? The high-level behavior: we prefer `preferred_model` if available, otherwise try fallbacks in order. BUT there are edge cases (dedicated capacity, force locks, and incompatible tokenizers) where routing differs — need the exact config to be precise.
maria: Quick note on SDK: current async streaming in python uses a client-side iterator; calling `stream.aclose()` (or cancelling the coroutine) will stop the client from reading more tokens but won't always send an immediate hard-cancel to the server. Server may keep producing until the request times out or the runtime triggers a cancellation policy. Docs should call that out.
elaine: Thanks. The PR is also failing docs preview / linkcheck in CI which is holding the merge. I'm mostly blocked on runtime wording and the SDK cancel caveat before we mark it approved.
ci-bot: build/docs-preview #824 failed: linkcheck error in docs/guides/model-routing.md: code fence lint. Full log: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/824/logs
alex: I can take the runtime question. Short answer: hosted uses routing policy -> preferred then fallbacks. Dedicated can be configured with `force_model_lock` which causes the runtime to refuse fallback. Private (on-prem) inherits whatever the customer's runtime set. That said, there is a tricky bit: if a fallback has a different tokenizer / special tokens, the token accounting shown in the API response may reflect the *served* model's tokenization, which can confuse users. Might be worth a small note.
nada: (ada) small correction: the reviewer assigned wants to know if this is a docs-only clarification or if it changes expected app behavior. If it's the latter we need a deprecation/compat note.
samir: I'm going to run a short repro across hosted/dedicated with the exact snippet. Elaine — can you paste the PR snippet and a minimal repro command? I'll run tests and post exact wording.
elaine: Pasted below — minimal repro to run locally against staging runtime:
```
# excerpt from docs PR #482
routing:
  preferred_model: "redwood-7b"
  fallback_models:
    - "redwood-2b-quant"
    - "gptx-lite"
# SDK snippet (python async streaming):
async with client.stream("/v1/generate", json=payload) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk)
    # user cancels here -> `await stream.aclose()` in example
```
Run: curl -X POST $STAGING_URL/api/repro -d @payload.json -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY"
samir: Thanks — ran hosted + dedicated (with force_model_lock=false) + dedicated (force_model_lock=true) quickly. Observations: hosted = prefer redwood-7b, fall back in order. Dedicated with `force_model_lock=false` behaves like hosted. Dedicated with `force_model_lock=true` rejects the request if preferred_model isn't on that pool (403/ModelUnavailable). Private depends on customer config (we can't assert). Important edge: when fallback is quantized variant with different tokenizer, the runtime serves the fallback model but the API's reported token counts are computed based on the served model; you should add a note about token accounting variance. Also: there is no transparent token-conversion between models — meaning prompts may token-split differently.
maria: On the SDK cancel semantics I tested: `await stream.aclose()` closes the HTTP connection from the client side. The server receives TCP FIN but depending on runtime batching/queueing it might already be producing tokens; there is no guarantee the server will immediately stop execution and free GPU until runtime cancellation loop runs. So docs should say: "client cancel may not imply immediate server-side termination — final tokens may still be produced and billed". Example snippet suggestion:
```
# recommend showing cancel + note
async with client.stream("/v1/generate", json=payload) as stream:
    try:
        async for chunk in stream:
            print(chunk)
            if should_cancel():
                await stream.aclose()
                break
    finally:
        # server may still be finishing work; use short timeout on server if you expect hard abort semantics
        pass
```
ada: That wording sounds fine. One more ask: can we include a short matrix table in the doc: hosted / dedicated (force lock on/off) / private with bullets describing routing behavior? Reviewer wants an explicit line for enterprise support.
elaine: I'll add a 3-row bullet matrix + the token-accounting caveat and the SDK cancel note. CI linkcheck failure fixed in branch (fixing code fence), but I'm keeping the merge on hold until we confirm your suggested sentences.
samir: Suggested language you can paste into the PR: "Routing behavior: 1) Hosted: attempts preferred_model, falls back through fallback_models in order. 2) Dedicated: if the pool includes preferred_model, it is used; if `force_model_lock` is true and preferred_model is not present, the request is rejected. If `force_model_lock` is false, behavior matches hosted. 3) Private: follows customer runtime configuration — contact platform ops for specifics." Also add: "Note: token counts and tokenization may differ between preferred and fallback models; reported token usage reflects the model that ultimately serves the request."
maria: And SDK snippet caption: "Client-side cancel closes the connection but does not guarantee immediate termination of server-side work — additional tokens may be produced and billed. To enforce early termination, configure server-side execution timeouts or use Dedicated pools with cancel policies."
elaine: Perfect — I'm pasting both suggested paragraphs into the PR and will re-run CI. If CI / linkcheck passes I'll remove the hold and merge. Thanks all :thumbsup: 
ci-bot: build/docs-preview #825 started: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/825
elaine: CI passed and wording accepted. Removing merge hold and merging now. Thanks everyone! :party-popper:
